_comment: Flashcards de la Parte 2 del NIE. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

cards.back: Causing another to apprehend immediate unlawful force (words/silence can suffice – Ireland)
Intentional or reckless application of unlawful force; can be indirect (Haystead)
Only that of the assault/battery; no foresight of harm needed (Savage; Roberts)
Hurt/injury interfering with health or comfort, more than transient (Miller); psychiatric injury; cutting hair (DPP v Smith 2006)
Break in both layers of the skin (JCC v Eisenhower); inner skin of mouth counts
Really serious harm (DPP v Smith 1961); look at whole injuries and victim (Bollom)
Intention or recklessness as to SOME harm (Cunningham; Savage/Parmenter)
Intent to do GBH OR to resist/prevent lawful apprehension – specific intent, life max
No consent to ABH or worse, except recognised exceptions
Sport, surgery, tattooing/piercing, rough horseplay (Jones), informed risk of infection
Consent to serious harm for sexual gratification is no defence (ABH+)
England: only for common assault/battery – not ABH+. Abolished in Wales (2022)
Reasonable force in circumstances as D believed them; householder: grossly disproportionate never reasonable
Threat without lawful excuse, intending the person to fear it would be carried out
